results.content: In economics, **shrinkflation**, also known as **package downsizing**, **weight-out**, and **price pack architecture** is the process of available products shrinking in size or quantity while the prices remain the same. This sometimes does not affect inflation measures such as the consumer price index or Retail Price Index, i.e. it might not increase in the cost of a basket of retail goods and services,*[citation needed*] but many indicators of price levels and thus inflation are linked to units of volume or weight of products, so that shrinkflation also affects the statistically represented inflation figures. 1.
